correctness.rationale: For a general codimension-c complete-intersection surface, Corollary 2.10 of the inspected source gives EDdeg as the degree product times the sum of complete homogeneous terms through degree two. Writing x_i=d_i-1 gives the exact factor 1+T+(T^2+Q)/2. A balancing move (x,y)->(x+1,y-1) with delta=y-x-1>0 changes the pair product from B to B+delta and the symmetric factor from A to A-delta, so the ED-degree change is a positive outside product times delta(A-B-delta). Since B+delta=(x+2)y and A>(x+2)y, every balancing move is strict. Repetition proves the unique balanced maximum; reversing moves proves the unique one-heavy minimum. The packaged exact checker independently verifies 425 multidegrees across 45 fixed-sum families and 933 admissible elementary balancing moves in its stated range.

value.rationale: ED degree measures algebraic complexity of the nearest-point problem. The theorem gives a complete sharp range over every complete-intersection surface with fixed codimension and fixed canonical polarization exponent, identifying both extremizers uniquely. It reveals a structural balancing law and a dimension-sensitive boundary rather than an isolated computation or arbitrary slice.
